heard: An exposed astronaut will not freeze instantly in space. Movies show human bodies freezing solid or exploding in a vacuum, but space is a giant insulator, so heat leaves very slowly. Your elastic skin easily keeps your body from bursting. Instead, your lungs instantly reverse and pull oxygen from your blood. In a NASA vacuum test, engineer Jim LeBlanc lost suit pressure. He felt the saliva on his tongue boil right before blacking out. Cold never gets the chance to kill you first.
